findings.issue_text: packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:149 — Backup-code consumption uses a non-atomic read-modify-write, allowing concurrent logins to redeem the same code or overwrite updates for different codes and restore consumed codes.

packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — tabIndex={-1} removes the password-visibility button from keyboard navigation across all PasswordField instances, preventing keyboard-only users from operating it.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

per_golden_matches.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment - the non-atomic read-modify-write pattern for backup codes that allows concurrent logins to use the same backup code multiple times. Both comments point to the race condition where two concurrent requests could both pass the backup code check before either updates the database, effectively allowing a single backup code to be used more than once. The candidate even mentions the same file location and describes the same security weakness.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/components/form/inputs/Input.tsx:49 — tabIndex={-1} removes the password-visibility button from keyboard navigation across all PasswordField instances, preventing keyboard-only users from operating it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows tabIndex={-1} being added to the password visibility toggle button in PasswordField component. This removes the button from keyboard tab navigation, which is a real accessibility issue. Keyboard-only users will not be able to tab to this button to toggle password visibility. This is a verifiable defect that affects all PasswordField instances across the application.
